records.name: Madagascar
records.current_summary: Madagascar demands real caution from trans visitors. Same-sex conduct is legal — unusual for the region — but France 24 documents that LGBT people must hide to keep jobs and live in peace; there is no LGR, no anti-discrimination law, and no visible community outside Antananarivo. No documented police targeting pattern.
records.current_outOfScope: Thin data; legal but closeted profile.

sources.claim: France 24 'Focus' report (Aug 2024): 'LGBT people in Madagascar forced to hide their sexuality' — although homosexuality is not illegal, it is widely considered socially unacceptable; many hide to keep jobs and live in peace, developing their own networks and coded language.

US State Department 2011 Human Rights Report for Madagascar: documents the post-coup regime, unlawful killings, and 'societal discrimination and violence against women, persons with disabilities, and the lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender (LGBT) community'.

BBC News Pidgin overview of decriminalisation in Africa (July 2020): Madagascar entry — same-sex activity legal only from age 21 under the Penal Code (under-21 same-sex acts remain offences); no recognition of same-sex marriage or civil unions; regional context as ~22 of 53 African states had moved to decriminalise.

Queer In The World Madagascar guide (updated 3 December 2023): same-sex activity legal for over-21s but LGBT people face discrimination and lack civic rights such as marriage and adoption; the legal framework is limited in progress compared with other countries.

Erasing 76 Crimes (17 July 2025): in Madagascar’s fourth UPR (January 2025, 235 recommendations) the government rejected UN recommendations to combat anti-LGBT violence and hate speech and to equalise the age of consent; six Malagasy organisations (Queer Place, Mifoha Olo Mazoto, Divers’ Unité, Justice Égalitaire, Men Engage, Madagascar LGBT+) protested that "Refusing to act is to endorse impunity and condone violence."

Rights in Exile (AsyLex) Madagascar resources: Penal Code Article 331 sets a different age of consent for same-sex acts (indecent-assault band of five to ten years’ imprisonment); documents general societal discrimination against LGBTQI+ people plus state-protection capacity, case law and supporting organisations.
